notes: Scan 120 is author folio 59, with separate pencil foliation 119 at lower left. The line_count is 22: sixteen prose lines plus six displayed or diagram lines; overlapping cancelled starts and marginal numbers are not counted as extra lines.

The opening is a continuation beginning où σ. The page asserts local-immersion/local-monomorphism and relative-codimension consequences and then adds (180), codim(D_d to D_0)=d. The preceding diagram or definition of σ is outside this assigned page, so those geometric implications were not independently proved here.

Formula (181) visibly uses an exclamation-mark exponent, not a prime. The stem and detached dot are preserved even though this may conflict with an expected interpretation of the expression. The supplied notation distinguishes the exclamation-mark object from the branch-cover notation; it does not authorize silently changing the ink.

Conditional mathematical reading test for (181): if D_d^! here denotes a principal symmetric-group S_d torsor and I_x has d elements, a geometric torsor fibre has d! elements whereas the full power set P(I_x) has 2^d. Already d=1 gives 1 versus 2. This checks the compatibility of those explicit assumptions, not the intended global statement, and is not a reason to replace the clearly written ! by a prime.

In (182), x was placed in D_d but the covering is literally written as above D_1. Germs at x require a specified point of the stated base. No identification or image in D_1 is supplied at this spot, so this is a scoped base-type mismatch to flag, not to repair. The later points x_i in D_1 do not make the earlier written base D_1 into D_d.

The chain writes s_i as arrows with source D_d after discussing germs of sections at x. No shrinkage of the base or global existence of sections is added to the transcription. The equality of composites with the canonical i_d map is recorded as the manuscript claim; this isolated page does not provide the definitions needed for an independent proof.

The pale horizontal trace after (D_{d,1})_x is uneven, unconnected and much lighter than the ink. It is not transcribed as H’s dash. The separate dark comma is retained. No deletion is inferred from that trace.

The live canonical target X is legible as two long diagonals over an old D-shaped form. The old subscript remains uncertain. The lower can label, the crowded chain subscript, the cancelled NB/Et and cancelled (181), and the compressed images are deliberately left open.

C and H differ typographically between calligraphic and fraktur power-set P. That is not treated as a source-letter change; the established C macro is retained. H editorial notes are not source text, but the real cancelled ink mentioned by its note on the two bottom formulas is explicitly represented.

Root check MC120-R independently compared the same conditional interpretations at d=2: an S_2 torsor has2 elements while the full subset set of a2-element set has4. The four subsets are the empty set, the two singletons and the whole set. This corroborates the limited cardinality incompatibility without changing the clearly written exclamation mark or claiming a refutation under every possible intended meaning of P.
